newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL Energy jumps after Noverco deal.
newsitem.headline: IPL Energy jumps after Noverco deal.

text.p: Shares of IPL Energy Inc jumped on Wednesday as investors applauded its deal to buy into Quebec's Noverco Inc, a move analysts said put it in the vanguard of convergence of numerous energy services.
Calgary-based IPL, operator of Canada's main crude oil pipeline system and owner of big Ontario utility Consumers Gas Co, climbed 1.15 to 49 in early Toronto Stock Exchange trade.
IPL's C$330 million deal to acquire shares of Noverco was announced on Tuesday, but the company's stock was halted all day. Noverco's main asset is an 80 percent stake in Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP.
Besides giving IPL a big stake in Quebec and Maritimes gas distribution, it also puts it in partnership with Hydro-Quebec, one of North America's biggest electricity producers and distributors.
IPL said on Tuesday it would acquire 32 percent of Noverco held by Caisse de depot et placement du Quebec for C$330 million.
In a related deal, IPL would issue to Noverco 6 million shares, or 8 percent, of its common stock for proceeds of C$287 million.
IPL also said it would sell to Noverco an option to buy 1.5 million more shares in mid-1998 at C$51 each. That would bring Noverco's ownership interest in IPL to 10 percent.
Sam Kanes, analyst with ScotiaMcleod in Toronto, said the deal was only the latest of numerous new forays for IPL into various non-regulated energy businesses.
"IPL's moved from nowhere three months ago to everywhere in the country," said Kanes, who moved his recommendation to "strong buy" from "hold" with a 12-month target price of 55 on Wednesday.

Other recent deals launching the company into new markets included a jump into Ontario's retail gas distribution business, a joint venture with Nova Scotia Power to pursue gas distribution opportunities, an alliance with Houston-based NGC Corp, an oil marketing venture with Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and a new Alberta heavy oil pipeline project with Suncor Energy Inc.
"It had so many deals announced so quickly that it's like they were lining all these ducks together in a way that's pretty damned impressive," Kanes said.
IPL has said the deal, in which Noverco also takes a stake in IPL, would add 12 cents a share to the company's annual earnings. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
